title: Set up benefits
summary: Research and enroll company in health insurance, dental, vision, 401k, and other benefits.

parts.title: Research benefits options
parts.guidance: Define the workforce, work locations, benefits goals and employer budget. Compare possible structures with the benefits adviser, including employee costs, administration and existing coverage or contract commitments. Gather only the workforce information needed for that assessment through private channels. Bring the decision makers the meaningful tradeoffs and unknowns before requesting specific plans or promising coverage.

parts.title: Get quotes from providers
parts.guidance: Request comparable proposals using the same workforce assumptions, desired benefits and contribution budget. Evaluate standalone quotes or a PEO arrangement with the employment and administrative responsibilities clearly separated. Limit recipient disclosures to the information needed for the quote. Compare coverage conditions, effective dates, employee costs and exclusions before recommending a route.

options.title: Default — Get quotes from providers
options.summary: Request standalone benefit quotes using consistent workforce assumptions and desired coverage. Compare the actual terms, employer and employee costs, implementation conditions and renewal basis with the adviser. Resolve differences that prevent a fair comparison before choosing a plan. Base coverage communications on accepted plan terms and confirmed enrollment.

options.title: PEO-bundled benefits
options.summary: Compare the PEO’s employment arrangement, benefit plans, service duties, fees and exit terms with standalone alternatives. Review actual coverage and total cost with the adviser, including responsibilities the company retains. Settle the commercial and legal arrangement before committing to the PEO. Carry the reviewed eligibility rules and enrollment conditions into implementation.
options.when: You want benefits bundled with payroll via co-employment - trading control for speed

parts.title: Select plans and negotiate
parts.guidance: Compare the quoted plan documents with employee needs, provider access, deductibles, exclusions and contribution costs. Clarify price assumptions, renewal terms and administrative work with the adviser. Take material tradeoffs to the benefits and budget decision makers before committing to the chosen arrangement. Resolve implementation conditions before communicating enrollment dates or coverage promises.

parts.title: Configure benefits in Gusto
parts.guidance: Configure the selected plans using their actual eligibility, contribution and coverage-start rules. Reconcile employee classes and deduction codes with payroll and the benefits administrator. Check representative enrollment outcomes against the plan documents and resolve discrepancies before activation. After elections begin, compare system records with accepted carrier or administrator enrollment so a saved setting is not mistaken for active coverage.

parts.title: Announce to team and open enrollment
parts.guidance: Explain the approved plans, employee costs, enrollment dates and support options using the plan materials. Check the audience and required notices with the benefits administrator, then give employees a working enrollment route. Clarify how they make elections or record waivers and where dependent or health information belongs. Address access problems early enough for employees to make their choices.

parts.title: Employees enroll
parts.guidance: Employees review the official materials and enter their own elections, dependent information or waivers in the enrollment system. Help with access and process questions without choosing coverage for them. Reconcile accepted elections with administrator or carrier confirmations and payroll deductions, following up on rejected or missing records. Give employees a way to check their own coverage result.

metadata.supportReason: Gusto handles benefits enrollment. Plan selection and broker negotiation require human decisions.

geoNotes.summary: The statutory floor is ESI health cover for lower-wage employees, EPF retirement, and gratuity; on top, a group mediclaim policy is the standard startup benefit — group health cover for employees has been an IRDAI expectation since 2020.

The NHS makes health insurance a perk rather than table stakes; the mandatory piece is pension auto-enrolment, and any private medical or similar benefit is a taxable benefit-in-kind reported to HMRC (P11D or payrolling).

Health, pension, care and unemployment insurance are statutory and ride payroll — there is no benefits enrollment project; the discretionary layer is a bAV pension offer (mandatory to offer) and perks like the Deutschlandticket or company fitness.

Every employer must provide a mutuelle — complementary health insurance at least 50% employer-funded — plus prévoyance cover for cadres; both plug into payroll's DSN rather than an open-enrollment season.

Statutory social security (pensions, sickness, unemployment) rides payroll and the SNS provides universal healthcare — there is no benefits-enrollment project; the common extras are meal allowance and private health insurance as perks.

Provincial medicare covers care, so the real project is the extended-health layer: group benefits (dental, vision, drugs, disability) through an insurer, with CRA's taxable-benefit rules deciding what lands on the T4.
